title: Hybrid v3 safety tuner and recovery playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Intermittent latency and OOM regressions observed after enabling FlashAttention v3 for mixed-precision decoder workloads. This ticket scopes a mitigations-first approach: implement a lightweight safety tuner that adjusts per-layer kernel selection thresholds at startup and under pressure, add automated recovery actions for transitory regressions (circuit breaker + fallback to v2), and produce an operator playbook for on-call and release engineers.
background: After rolling out v3 on canary in region-us-west, production telemetry shows a ~12% p99 latency spike for single-turn decode workloads and rare OOMs during high-concurrency spikes. Initial root cause signals point to v3 micro-tiling selection and per-layer workspace estimation being brittle for certain sequence-length distributions and mixed quantization profiles. Existing kernel selector assumes warm KV cache and steady batch shapes; coldstart and bursty loads expose selection instability.
acceptance_criteria: Safety tuner service integrated into kernel selector that updates kernel selection scoring in <=50ms per config epoch
Automated rollback path: request-level fallback to FlashAttention v2 when p99 latency > baseline + 20% or OOMs occur more than 3x in 5m window
Canary harness that simulates coldstart bursts and reproduces observed p99 spike deterministically
Operational runbook describing detection, mitigation, and postmortem checklist for regression incidents
Telemetry: add per-request kernel-choice histogram and memory-estimation-errors metric; dashboards show root-cause signals within 5m
reproduction_steps: Deploy hybrid-v3-canary in us-west with same VM/GPU types as incidents (A100-40GB), enable per-layer v3 for decoder layers 6-12
Run traffic replay from 2026-03-02 03:00-03:30 UTC with original seq length distribution (attach replay script: gs://redwood-replays/2026-03-02-burst.tar.gz)
Use synthetic storm generator to create 60-120 concurrent short-turn requests with randomized prompt prefixes to exercise KV cold paths
Collect runtime logs with kernel-choice tracing and workspace_estimate vs actual_allocated values (sampling 100% for offending shard)
Observe p50/p95/p99 and memory-growth; correlate with kernel-choice transitions
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Preliminary profiling shows v3 tiler overestimates workspace for certain head count shapes leading to fallback eviction churn (~30% extra allocs)
2026-03-12: Reproducer found when interleaving short (10 tokens) and long (1024 tokens) requests in the same worker; selector oscillates between v3 microtiles and v2 fallback causing latency jitter
2026-03-12: Memory sampling reveals transient spikes ~1.2GB above baseline prior to OOM; correlation with layer 9/10 activations and mixed-precision quant boundaries
2026-03-13: Tested heuristic: add hysteresis to selector (require 3 consecutive samples favoring v3 before switching) — reduced oscillation but increased p50 on some workloads
Decision: implement tunable safety tuner that learns safe thresholds from observed allocation errors and warmup signals, rather than hard-coded hysteresis
design_decisions: Safety tuner will run as part of runtime initialization and continuously adapt at low priority (10s epoch): it will adjust score deltas and minimum confidence required for v3 selection
Tuner will use three signals: workspace_estimate_error, kernel_switch_rate, and decode_latency_trend. Each signal mapped to a delta in score between v2 and v3 for the layer and shape bucket
Fallback policy: request-scoped circuit breaker with sliding window; if >3 OOMs or 5s of sustained p99 degradation, mark v3 unhealthy for that worker and replace with v2 for 60s
Canary rollout: staged enabling at 1%, 5%, 10% with canary prober that injects cold KV prefixes and bursty concurrency
Observability: emit 'tuner_decision' events including reason, affected_layer, shape_bucket, delta_applied and keep last 100 events in ringbuffer for fast diagnostics
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (3d): Instrument kernel selector to surface workspace_estimate_error, kernel_switch_rate, and per-layer latency deltas to telemetry; add lightweight sampling hooks
Phase 2 (4d): Implement safety tuner library with config-driven thresholds; expose feature flag runtime.hybrid_safety_tuner = true
Phase 3 (2d): Implement worker-local circuit breaker and request-level fallback that prefers v2 when breaker tripped; update API to include kernel_hint for debugging
Phase 4 (2d): Build canary prober and replay harness; author regression test that fails when p99 increases >10% against baseline
Phase 5 (2d): Operationalize dashboards and runbook; schedule small canary rollout with SRE supervision
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: tuner mis-tuning could prefer v2 excessively increasing cost. Mitigation: cost-aware regularizer in tuner that penalizes downgrades beyond target delta
Risk: added telemetry overhead. Mitigation: default sampling 1% on prod, 100% on canary; use aggregated counters for histograms
Risk: fallback thrash under flapping signals. Mitigation: exponential backoff in circuit breaker and per-layer cooldown windows
Risk: operator confusion during rollout. Mitigation: clear runbook pages and one-click rollback (disable runtime.hybrid_safety_tuner)
Risk: interactions with quantization profiles. Mitigation: include quantization_profile as a shape_bucket dimension in tuner inputs
observability_changes: Trace additions: annotate traces with kernel_choice and tuner_decision ids to correlate latency spikes
Dashboards: canary health with p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_rate heatmap, workspace_estimate_error trend lines
Alerts: p99 delta > 20% v.s. baseline for 5m (warning at 10%), OOM rate > 1/min per worker
Log sampling: keep 100 tuner_decision events per worker (ringbuffer) with compression to GCS for postmortem
rollback_and_recovery: Immediate mitigation: enable runtime flag runtime.force_kernel_v2=true for affected region/workers (one CLI toggle)
Automatic: worker-local circuit breaker that gracefully swaps to v2 for 60s and retries inflight requests with a token bucket to prevent stampede
Post-incident: collect replay snapshot and escalate to kernel-team with attachable synthetic trace
Long-term: schedule a follow-up ticket to harden v3 workspace estimator and to introduce a cross-worker consensus on safe kernel selection for multi-tenant servers
